Back Privacy In one sentence FitHub collects no usage data. There is no account system, no crash reporting, no analytics, and no ad SDK. Network requests Requests only happen when you tap something, and every one of them is a read: GitHub public API: browsing repositories, search, releases and READMEs GitHub release downloads: fetching the package you tapped The device-code authorization page: only reached from "Sign in with GitHub", to exchange the approval for an access token The WebDAV host you configured: only contacted when subscription sync is on Everything works without signing in. The cost is GitHub\'s unauthenticated rate limit: 60 requests per hour. What stays on this device Browsing history: which repositories you opened, which packages you parsed, what you installed through FitHub Local scan results: the list of installed apps and their signing fingerprints Your subscriptions and preferences Your GitHub access token (after signing in) — stored encrypted in the Android Keystore, never in plaintext All of it lives in the app\'s private directory. It is never uploaded and never part of WebDAV sync — syncing it would put browsing history on another device that never happened here, and that is not your data. Clear the browsing history or uninstall the app to delete it. Downloaded packages Downloaded packages go to the system cache directory, which Android clears on its own when space runs short. FitHub does not repackage them and does not alter the bytes you downloaded — it is exactly the one file from the GitHub release. Runtime dependencies These libraries ship inside the package, each under its own license: AndroidX Jetpack Compose / Material 3 — Apache License 2.0 Ktor — Apache License 2.0 kotlinx.serialization — Apache License 2.0 multiplatform-markdown-renderer (mikepenz) — Apache License 2.0 They are all Apache-2.0, which is compatible with this project\'s MIT License. Data sources All repository information, release assets and README content come from the GitHub API and remain the property of their respective authors.
